## Conference overview

*Preview by Adam Burke, p. 187. Reproduced in full.*


> Recently, Conference USA has been the proving ground for teams moving up from the FCS ranks to the FBS world.

> This season, that is not the case, as the new teams are in the Mountain West and MAC.

> However, with Louisiana Tech off to the Sun Belt and UTEP to the Mountain West, Conference USA goes from 12 teams down to 10.

> This is absolutely the weakest conference in college football.

> There were 136 FBS teams last season.

> Jeff Sagarin’s end- of-season rankings had four teams in the conference 158th or lower.

> Four other teams were ranked 120th or lower.

> Ironically, the top two teams as ranked by Sagarin - Western Kentucky and Louisiana Tech - weren’t even involved in the conference championship game.

> Kennesaw State won 19-15 over Jacksonville State in that one.

> It was a truly impressive season for Kennesaw State.

> The Owls fired their longtime head coach during their first season as a FBS member in 2024 and hired Jerry Mack, who was a running backs coach in the NFL the season prior and had only been a head coach at NC Central in the mid-2010s.

> With that win, the Owls avenged their only conference regular-season loss and then got pumped by Western Michigan in the Myrtle Beach Bowl.

> The Gamecocks may be able to avenge that title game loss, as they look to be a contender once again behind second-year head coach Charles Kelly, as the team lost head coach Rich Rodriguez, had very few returning starters, and still went 7-1 in league action before the loss in the title game.

> Arguably the biggest storyline of the season is whether or not Liberty will bounce back.

> After a 21-5 start, including a College Football Playoff appearance, it all fell apart for Jamey Chadwell, as the Flames went just 4-8 last season.

> Liberty (+260) is the conference favorite over Western Kentucky (+280), who has the longest-tenured coach in the conference as Tyson Helton starts his eighth season.

> With Jacksonville State (+450) and Delaware (7-1) as the others lined in single digits, this looks to be a wide-open Group of Six conference again. conference usa

## Quarterback themes


**From the conference preview (p. 187):**

> *Not addressed in guide.*


**From the team pages in this conference** — 10 of 10 teams' pages address this theme. A sample follows; Phase 3 carries the full treatment team by team.


- **Delaware Fightin’ Blue Hens** (p. 188) — It all starts with QB Nick Minicucci, who threw for nearly 3,700 yards with a 23/7 TD/INT ratio.

- **FIU Golden Panthers** (p. 191) — Unfortunately for Simmons, his leading QB, RB, WR, tackler, and defensive back are all gone, so he and his staff had a lot of work to do in the offseason.

- **Jacksonville State Gamecocks** (p. 192) — We’ll see what Year 2 has in store, as the Gamecocks will be without Cam Cook, who ran for 1,659 yards, but will fully turn the keys of the offense over to QB Caden Creel, a 1,000-yard rusher himself who also threw for over 1,500 yards.

- **Kennesaw State Owls** (p. 194) — A lot of players left in light of Bohannon’s departure, but Jerry Mack got to work, quickly rebuilding the roster and he hit a home run with QB Amari Odom, who stabilized the offense and gave them a dualthreat component.

- **Liberty Flames** (p. 196) — They had more interceptions than passing touchdowns, didn’t have sacks or takeaways on defense, and didn’t seem to have much leadership.

- **Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders** (p. 198) — We’ll see if Scelfo can build on some late-season offensive gains under QB Roman Gagliano, who stuck around with the program despite opening some eyes over the final three games.

- **Missouri State Bears** (p. 200) — Perhaps Woods turns Belin or Locklear into a quality starting QB, but this is a team with major questions in the trenches and that is a lot to overlook given the uncertainty at the most important position on the field.

- **New Mexico State Aggies** (p. 202) — The job that Jerry Kill did in Las Cruces seems to get more and more impressive with each passing day.

**From the team pages in this conference** — 10 of 10 teams' pages address this theme. A sample follows; Phase 3 carries the full treatment team by team.


- **Delaware Fightin’ Blue Hens** (p. 188) — Whether that bowl game win had something to do with it or not, Delaware is in really good shape from a returning production standpoint, especially relative to their C-USA peers.

- **FIU Golden Panthers** (p. 191) — Unfortunately for Simmons, his leading QB, RB, WR, tackler, and defensive back are all gone, so he and his staff had a lot of work to do in the offseason.

- **Jacksonville State Gamecocks** (p. 192) — With Rich Rod back at West Virginia where it all started, the Gamecocks made what turned out to be a savvy hire of Kelly, who was an assistant here way back in the mid-90s.

- **Kennesaw State Owls** (p. 195) — Rickie Collins transferred in from Syracuse and Landon Varnes was a JUCO starter with 31 TD passes against 14 picks last season at Mississippi Gulf Coast.

- **Liberty Flames** (p. 196) — As Chadwell begins Year 4 with a new DC, a bounce back is expected.

- **Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders** (p. 198) — A very important Year 3 for head coach Derek Mason is on the horizon, as back-to-back 3-9 seasons have not inspired much confidence in the direction of the program.

- **Missouri State Bears** (p. 200) — Former SMU OC Casey Woods is now the head coach and returning production is hard to find on the depth chart, as a lot of players followed head coach Ryan Beard to Coastal Carolina or found homes elsewhere.

- **New Mexico State Aggies** (p. 202) — Aside from Kill’s 7-6 and 10-5 campaigns, the program has one other winning season (2017) dating back to 2002.

## Transfer-portal themes


**From the conference preview (p. 187):**

> *Not addressed in guide.*


**From the team pages in this conference** — 10 of 10 teams' pages address this theme. A sample follows; Phase 3 carries the full treatment team by team.


- **Delaware Fightin’ Blue Hens** (p. 189) — He kept him as the DC, but you wonder about his allegiance to him if the defense falters again in Year 2, especially with three of their four leading tacklers back and a few FBS-level transfers.

- **FIU Golden Panthers** (p. 191) — It wouldn’t be terribly surprising to see Kohl in something of a timeshare with Delaware transfer Zach Marker or freshman DJ Alexander, with the latter two as bigger running threats.

- **Jacksonville State Gamecocks** (p. 192) — This was a much more efficient offense with Creel at the helm as opposed to Rutgers/Kentucky transfer Gavin Wimsatt and that means there’s a lot of hope for this group, even if a new stud running back needs to emerge.

- **Kennesaw State Owls** (p. 195) — Rickie Collins transferred in from Syracuse and Landon Varnes was a JUCO starter with 31 TD passes against 14 picks last season at Mississippi Gulf Coast.

- **Liberty Flames** (p. 197) — Chadwell did get former Chanticleer Ethan Vasko to transfer in, but that didn’t really work out well, as he posted a 10/12 TD/INT ratio, threw for under 2,000 yards, and had just 2.6 yards per carry on 100 attempts.

- **Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders** (p. 198) — I’ll give Mason the benefit of the doubt that after his third portal and freshmen classes that he has players that better fit what he wants to do on defense.

- **Missouri State Bears** (p. 201) — Duke transfer Henry Belin and UTEP transfer Skyler Locklear are the two QB newcomers via the portal, along with holdovers Cole Feuerbacher and Elijah Leonard.

- **New Mexico State Aggies** (p. 202) — Depth was a huge issue last season and looks to be again, as 247Sports does have the program with 26 portal players, but the seventh-ranked class out of 10 teams.

## Historical and situational notes


**From the conference preview (p. 187):**

> There were 136 FBS teams last season.
>
> — *conference preview, p. 187*

> The Owls fired their longtime head coach during their first season as a FBS member in 2024 and hired Jerry Mack, who was a running backs coach in the NFL the season prior and had only been a head coach at NC Central in the mid-2010s.
>
> — *conference preview, p. 187*

> After a 21-5 start, including a College Football Playoff appearance, it all fell apart for Jamey Chadwell, as the Flames went just 4-8 last season.
>
> — *conference preview, p. 187*


**From the team pages in this conference** — 10 of 10 teams' pages address this theme. A sample follows; Phase 3 carries the full treatment team by team.


- **Delaware Fightin’ Blue Hens** (p. 188) — For Delaware to finish last season with a bowl victory was a huge one for the trophy case, as Ryan Carty’s Fightin’ Blue Hens pulled the mild upset of Louisiana in the 68 Ventures Bowl.

- **FIU Golden Panthers** (p. 190) — An unsung hero in the 2025 coaching ranks was FIU’s Willie Simmons, who took the team bowling for the first time since 2019.

- **Jacksonville State Gamecocks** (p. 193) — Last season, Cook was a bell cow, racking up 295 rush attempts and 16 rushing touchdowns.

- **Kennesaw State Owls** (p. 194) — This was a team that went 2-10 as a first-year FBS member in 2024.

- **Liberty Flames** (p. 196) — Kennesaw State’s eight-win improvement was a shocker, but so was Liberty’s complete reversal of fortunes, going from 8-4 to 4-8, as head coach Jamey Chadwell posted his worst record since 2017 when he was the interim HC at Coastal Carolina while Joe Moglia tended to health issues and the Chanticleers went 3-9.

- **Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders** (p. 198) — A very important Year 3 for head coach Derek Mason is on the horizon, as back-to-back 3-9 seasons have not inspired much confidence in the direction of the program.

- **Missouri State Bears** (p. 200) — The 43-year-old Woods has worked under Gus Malzahn, Eli Drinkwitz, Rhett Lashlee, and his dad Sparky has been a ball coach since 1976.

- **New Mexico State Aggies** (p. 202) — Kill was the head coach of the Aggies in 2022 and 2023, leading them to a 17-11 record.
